nodes.summary: In a state $s$ of deferred acceptance with proposers $0, 1, \dots, n-1$, the chooser returns the least proposer $m$ who is free in $s$ and has made fewer than $n$ proposals in $s$, or no proposer if there is none.
nodes.title: Choosing the next proposer

nodes.summary: Let each proposer $m$ rank the $n$ receivers by a permutation $\sigma_m$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, where $\sigma_m(k)$ is his choice of rank $k$, let each receiver rank the $n$ proposers, and let $p_m$ be the number of proposals $m$ has made in the final state of deferred acceptance. Then $p_m \ge 1$, and the Gale-Shapley partner $\mu(m)$ of $m$ has rank $p_m - 1$ in his ranking, that is,…
nodes.title: A proposer's final partner is his last proposal

nodes.summary: Let the $n$ proposers and the $n$ receivers both be numbered $0, \dots, n-1$. Let each proposer $m$ have a strict total order $\lt _m$ of preference on the receivers and each receiver $w$ a strict total order $\lt _w$ of preference on the proposers, where $x \lt _m y$ means that $m$ prefers $x$ to $y$, and likewise for $\lt _w$. Then there are permutations $\sigma_m$ (one for each proposer $m$) and $\tau_w$ (one…
nodes.title: Gale-Shapley serves every preference profile with $n$ proposers and $n$ receivers

nodes.summary: For every strict total order $\prec$ on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ there is a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that, for all $a$ and $b$, $a \prec b$ holds exactly when $\sigma^{-1}(a) < \sigma^{-1}(b)$.
nodes.title: Every strict total order on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is given by a ranking

nodes.summary: A proposer $m$ is free in a state $s$ of deferred acceptance when no receiver holds $m$ in $s$.
nodes.title: Free proposer

nodes.summary: Let each of $n$ proposers rank the $n$ receivers, and each receiver rank the $n$ proposers, with rank $0$ the best. Deferred acceptance is the state reached from the initial state, in which no one has proposed and no receiver holds anyone, by repeating the following step at most $n^2$ times, stopping early once no proposer is both free and has made fewer than $n$ proposals: the least such proposer, having made $p$…
nodes.title: Deferred acceptance

nodes.summary: No stable matching gives a proposer a partner he prefers to his Gale-Shapley partner.
nodes.title: Proposer-optimality

nodes.summary: No stable matching gives a receiver a partner she likes less than her Gale-Shapley partner.
nodes.title: Receiver-pessimality

nodes.summary: Each proposer with the receiver who holds him at the end.
nodes.title: The Gale-Shapley matching

nodes.summary: Fix rankings of the $n$ receivers by each of $n$ proposers and of the proposers by each receiver. Let $s$ be a state of deferred acceptance that satisfies the invariant of deferred acceptance for these rankings, and suppose that no proposer is both free in $s$ and has made fewer than $n$ proposals in $s$. Then every proposer is held by some receiver in $s$.
nodes.title: When deferred acceptance stops, every proposer is held

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a state of deferred acceptance with $n$ proposers and $n$ receivers. If every proposer is held by some receiver in $s$, then every receiver holds some proposer in $s$.
nodes.title: Every receiver holds someone once every proposer is held

nodes.summary: The initial state with $n$ proposers and $n$ receivers: every proposer has made $0$ proposals and no receiver holds anyone.
nodes.title: Initial state of deferred acceptance

nodes.summary: Let each proposer $m$ have a ranking $\sigma_m$ of the $n$ receivers and each receiver $w$ a ranking $\tau_w$ of the $n$ proposers, where $\sigma_m(k)$ is the choice of $m$ of rank $k$ (rank $0$ is the best) and $\tau_w^{-1}(x)$ is the rank of $x$ for $w$. A state $s$ of deferred acceptance satisfies the invariant when: every proposer has made at most $n$ proposals; if $w$ holds $m$, then $m$ has made $k + 1$…
nodes.title: Invariant of deferred acceptance

nodes.summary: For $n$ proposers and $n$ receivers, each with a ranking of the other side, the perfect matching computed by deferred acceptance is stable for the strict preferences given by these rankings.
nodes.title: The Gale-Shapley matching is stable

nodes.summary: Let each proposer $m$ have a ranking $\sigma_m$ of the $n$ receivers ($\sigma_m(k)$ is the choice of $m$ of rank $k$, rank $0$ the best), and each receiver a ranking of the $n$ proposers. Let $s$ be a state of deferred acceptance satisfying the invariant, let $\nu$ be a perfect matching that is stable for the preferences given by the rankings, let $m$ be a proposer, and let $b$ be a natural number at most the…
nodes.title: Rejected proposals bound stable partners

nodes.summary: Given for each proposer $m$ a ranking $\sigma_m$ of the $n$ receivers ($\sigma_m(k)$ is the choice of $m$ of rank $k$, rank $0$ the best), the proposers' preference profile assigns to $m$ the strict total order in which $m$ prefers $w$ to $w'$ when $\sigma_m^{-1}(w) < \sigma_m^{-1}(w')$.
nodes.title: Proposers' preferences from rankings

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a state of deferred acceptance, $m$ a proposer and $w$ a receiver with ranking $\tau_w$ of the proposers ($\tau_w^{-1}(x)$ is the rank of $x$, rank $0$ the best). Then one of the following holds: $w$ holds nobody in $s$ and holds $m$ after $m$ proposes to her; or $w$ holds some $y$ in $s$ with $\tau_w^{-1}(m) < \tau_w^{-1}(y)$ and holds $m$ after $m$ proposes to her; or $w$ holds some $y$ in $s$ with…
nodes.title: Cases of the receiver's new holder

nodes.summary: In a state $s$ of deferred acceptance, the proposer whom receiver $w$ holds after proposer $m$ proposes to her is $m$ if she holds nobody in $s$ or ranks $m$ strictly better than her current holder $m'$ in her ranking, and $m'$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Receiver's holder after a proposal

nodes.summary: Let each proposer $m$ have a ranking $\sigma_m$ of the $n$ receivers and each receiver $w$ a ranking $\tau_w$ of the $n$ proposers, where $\sigma_m^{-1}(x)$ and $\tau_w^{-1}(x)$ are ranks ($0$ the best). If $\nu$ is a perfect matching that is stable for the preferences given by these rankings, there are no proposer $m$ and receiver $w$ with $\sigma_m^{-1}(w) < \sigma_m^{-1}(\nu(m))$ and…
nodes.title: A stable matching has no blocking pair

nodes.summary: For a strict total order $<$ on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the rank of an element $a$ is the number of elements $b$ with $b < a$ (the elements preferred to $a$), as an element of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.
nodes.title: Rank under a strict total order

nodes.summary: In a state $s$ of deferred acceptance with $n$ proposers and $n$ receivers, both numbered $0, \dots, n-1$, the partner of a proposer $m$ is the lowest-numbered receiver that holds $m$ in $s$; if no receiver holds $m$, it is the receiver numbered $m$ (a default value).
nodes.title: Proposer's partner

nodes.summary: In a state $s$ of deferred acceptance with $n$ proposers and $n$ receivers, both numbered $0, \dots, n-1$, the partner of a receiver $w$ is the proposer she holds in $s$; if she holds nobody, it is the proposer numbered $w$ (a default value).
nodes.title: Receiver's partner

nodes.summary: Fix, for each proposer, a ranking of the $n$ receivers and, for each receiver, a ranking of the $n$ proposers (rank $0$ is the first choice). Let $s$ be a state of deferred acceptance in which proposer $m$ has made $k$ proposals. If $k < n$, then $m$ proposes to the receiver $w$ of rank $k$ in his ranking: his number of proposals becomes $k + 1$, and $w$ now holds $m$ if she held nobody or ranks $m$ strictly above…
nodes.title: A proposal

nodes.summary: For a state $s$ of deferred acceptance with $n$ proposers and $n$ receivers, in which each proposer $m$ has made $k_m$ proposals, the number of proposals still available is $\sum_{m} \max(n - k_m, 0)$, the sum running over all $n$ proposers.
nodes.title: Remaining proposals

nodes.summary: Fix rankings for $n$ proposers and $n$ receivers, both numbered $0, \dots, n-1$. Starting from a state $s$ with a budget of $f$ proposals: if $f = 0$, or if no proposer is both free (held by no receiver) and has made fewer than $n$ proposals, the run returns $s$; otherwise the lowest-numbered such proposer makes a proposal, and the run continues from the resulting state with budget $f - 1$.
nodes.title: Running deferred acceptance

nodes.summary: A state of deferred acceptance with $n$ proposers and $n$ receivers, both numbered $0, \dots, n-1$, records for each proposer a natural number, the number of proposals he has made (his next proposal goes to his choice of that rank), and for each receiver either the proposer she currently holds or that she holds nobody.
nodes.title: Deferred-acceptance state

nodes.summary: For any rankings of the $n$ receivers by each of the $n$ proposers and of the proposers by each receiver, in the final state of deferred acceptance the numbers of proposals made by the proposers sum to at most $n \cdot n$.
nodes.title: Deferred acceptance makes at most n² proposals

nodes.summary: Fix rankings for $n$ proposers and $n$ receivers. If proposer $m$ has made fewer than $n$ proposals in a state $s$ of deferred acceptance, then after $m$ proposes, the total number of proposals made by all proposers is one more than in $s$.
nodes.title: A proposal adds one to the proposal count

nodes.summary: A permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, read as a ranking ($\sigma(k)$ is the $k$-th choice, $\sigma(0)$ the best), gives the strict total order on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ in which $a$ is preferred to $b$ when $\sigma^{-1}(a) < \sigma^{-1}(b)$.
nodes.title: Preference order of a ranking

nodes.summary: Given for each receiver $w$ a ranking $\sigma_w$ of the $n$ proposers (a permutation of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, with $\sigma_w(0)$ her first choice), the receivers' preference profile assigns to $w$ the preference order of $\sigma_w$: $w$ prefers $a$ to $b$ when $\sigma_w^{-1}(a) < \sigma_w^{-1}(b)$.
nodes.title: Receivers' preference profile from rankings

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
